body_markdown:
You might be cringing if you are a regular reader of Hagerty’s *According To You* series. That’s understandable, because we have been discussing both makeshift and DIY repairs for weeks now. But before we switch gears, let’s take a look at a lifetime of work done DIY-style. This idea came from a Hagerty Media commenter, so thanks to[norm1220 for pondering](https://www.hagerty.com/media/hagerty-community/what-diy-repair-saved-you-the-most-money/comment-page-4/#:~:text=Hey%20Sajeev%2C%20this%20could%20be%20your%20next%20article/question%3A%20how%20much%20does%20one%20think%20they%20have%20saved%20in%20total%20by%20all%20of%20the%20repairs%20they%20have%20done%3F%20Here%E2%80%99s%20another%3A%20which%20failed%20repair%20cost%20the%20most%3F%20(ohhh%2C%20I%20know%20mine!)) this notion in a previous episode:


> Although it’s a maintenance item, I pose the same question: what about oil changes? I’ve been doing them a looong time, and if allowed to add them up, I’m thinking it would easily be in the top-5 most saved $$$ list.


Norm brings up a good point, so let’s get to the heart of his thoughts:


> Hey Sajeev, this could be your next article/question: **how much does one think they have saved in total by all of the repairs they have done?**


I have binders full of receipts for all the cars I turn a wrench on, but doing the math on all that sounds like more trouble than it’s worth. (To my retirement portfolio!) I’ll guess that I’ve saved close to $150,000 in parts and labor expenses. Most of the savings came from price shopping for OEM parts (mostly on eBay from individuals lacking their own catalog/website), stripping down cars before paint, and the requisite oil changes since I got serious with cars in the late 1990s.

While I saved a lot of money on oil changes, the discounts received from DIY prep (before paint) and New-Old-Stock part procurement/installation (after paint) really stick in my mind. So tell us, dear reader: **how much have you saved in total with your DIY handiwork?**
